doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Morgan State and the Baltimore scene with Gary Bartz
summary: Only classical theory at college, but Baltimore's Royal Theater and Pennsylvania Avenue were alive with jazz; he played standards with Gary Bartz at the North End Lounge.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did they have any programs at that time that were — addressed jazz? Or were you more learning the classical theory and so forth?

Just basic classical theory. Because back then, when I was back there they hadn’t even started these jazz colleges and universities yet. But at that time in Baltimore, Maryland it was very, very musical. And all the jazz groups used to come down and play on Pennsylvania Avenue and so Baltimore was kind of like New York because you had the — New York had the Apollo Theater. And Baltimore, the same groups would come and do the Royal Theater in Baltimore, then they would go to Washington, DC and do the Howard Theater. And so music was everywhere between Washington and Baltimore, which is right together. And then actually Gary Bartz I had met, Gary Bartz is from Baltimore, so we both were what, 18, 19, 20? We used to hang out. And we ended up playing together in his father’s club called the North End Lounge, and so Baltimore was very musical back then.
What would your set list have been like, playing with Gary Bartz at that time?
Oh we were just doing standards you know. Just basic standards and what was it, what did I do, oh shoot, what did we do?
I forgot it. Then you know we’d do something like that
